learning_outcomes.text: Students know and understand essential boundary conditions and methods for the development of components and systems of the Internet of Things. They can reproduce the essential characteristics of different approaches.

Important aspects of the Internet of Things such as software and cloud platforms, sensors, and actuators are understood from an application and software development perspective. Boundary conditions such as input/output possibilities and energy (especially for energetically autonomous systems) are analyzed and incorporated into problem-solving. The potential of incorporating mathematics and computer science knowledge into small and smallest intelligent systems is understood. The handling of typical integration issues is correctly implemented.

Students who have successfully completed this module understand how to consider all aspects of embedding Internet of Things systems and Industry 4.0, including their distribution, interfaces, and resource-efficient implementation.

Students who have successfully completed this module possess knowledge about the essential aspects of developing Internet of Things (IoT) and Industry 4.0 systems and can apply this knowledge in the creation of concepts, architectures, and implementations.

Students who have successfully completed this module can analyze innovative products and new technological possibilities based on IoT and Industry 4.0. They understand how to implement these in terms of distribution, interfaces, and resource-efficient realization during development.

Students who have successfully completed this module can cooperate with groups from other disciplines and clearly explain their own technical aspects. They can, at various stages of group collaboration, structured summarize, document, and present the respective work results.

Students can adequately assess their individual qualification profile regarding the analysis and development of Internet of Things systems and in the field of Industry 4.0, and can differentiate and justify their technological and methodological decisions.

syllabus_topics: Application areas in private and professional sectors
Construction types and resource-efficient development of typical IoT devices
Components and methods for data acquisition and processing in IoT
Decentralized sensor data fusion, data aggregation, and reduction
Development of software for IoT systems
SW architectures for data storage and analysis in IoT
assessment_rules: The graded portfolio examination comprises 100 points, consisting of five practical work samples (APS) and one written project report (PSC). A maximum of 10 points can be achieved for each of the five APS, and a maximum of 60 points for the PSC. The practical work samples are 10-15 pages each, including source code. The PSC is 25-30 pages, including source code. The ungraded experimental work includes approximately 4-6 experiments.
